requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST tell agents that renaming or restructuring code in place, without changing behavior, needs no requirement review, but that the item's references move with it and the evidence that read it is reassessed.
rationale:
structural: The requirement `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.code_rename` says only that the `habeas-requirements` skill "MUST tell agents" three things. Renaming or restructuring code in place without changing behavior needs no requirement review. The item's references move with it. The evidence that read it is reassessed. This constrains what the skill's guidance says. It does not constrain how anything is built. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. The skill's text is the deliverable, so any structure that conveys the same guidance would satisfy it. Examples are a different section, different wording, or a separate file that the skill points to. No implementation root needs a reference. The supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, is the guidance document itself. Whether its text actually says the required things is a content-adequacy question and was not assessed here.

behavioral: `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.code_rename` is a documentation obligation on the `habeas-requirements` skill. The skill MUST tell agents four things. (a) Renaming or restructuring code in place needs no requirement review. (b) That holds when behavior is unchanged. (c) The item's references move with the code. (d) The evidence that read it is reassessed.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_needs_no_review_for_renaming_code_in_place]` carries the `{test}` marker. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper runs `assert_text` over `bundled_skill("habeas-requirements")`, which is `SKILL.md` plus its reference files with whitespace collapsed. `assert_text` asserts that the text contains the phrase and panics otherwise. The asserted sentence is "Restructuring code in place, including renaming an item, needs no requirement review, but references move with the code and the evidence is reassessed".

That one sentence covers (a), (c) and (d): in-place restructuring and renaming, no requirement review, references moving with the code, and evidence reassessed. The test targets the right skill. The sentence appears in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` in the Workflow section. Removing or reversing any clause would fail the assertion.

The sentence does not contain the words "without changing behavior". I treated (b) as implied by "restructuring code in place", which is behavior-preserving by definition. The same Workflow paragraph also sends behavior no requirement covers back to step 2. I did not count the missing wording as a test gap. If a reviewer reads (b) as needing its own wording, the skill text would need it first, and that is not a test-adequacy question.

No gaps found.
